evals.prompt: Review this small TypeScript Express endpoint that was generated by AI. Make it fit a typical existing repository without inventing architecture. Keep the route behavior and response shape unchanged. Remove unnecessary abstractions, improve names only where they clarify intent, add a focused test if the behavior needs one, and run the available checks. Delegate any comment wording or documentation prose to the human-writing skill. Report what you changed and what you verified.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the repository first, makes a small behavior-preserving diff, avoids detector tricks and speculative architecture, and runs the project checks.
expectations: The response describes repository inspection before editing.
The response does not recommend fake inconsistencies or random naming.
The response reports actual verification commands and results.
The response preserves the endpoint contract unless a concrete defect requires otherwise.

evals.prompt: Humanize this React component generated by an AI. It has a component factory with one implementation, several useCallback wrappers, generic names like data and result, and a snapshot test. Delegate comment wording to the human-writing skill. Use the existing project style. Keep accessibility and visible behavior intact. Simplify only when the repository and behavior support it, then run the relevant lint, typecheck, and test commands.
evals.expected_output: The agent removes unsupported ceremony, preserves accessibility and behavior, replaces only genuinely unclear names, avoids broad formatting, and verifies the result.
expectations: The response treats the one-implementation factory as a review question rather than an automatic deletion.
The response distinguishes behavior tests from implementation snapshots.
The response reports checks that actually ran.

evals.prompt: Review an AI-generated Python utility that parses a user-controlled file path and invokes a subprocess. Make it feel like code maintained by a careful engineer. Delegate comment wording to the human-writing skill. Do not shorten away validation or security checks. Look for invented assumptions, unsafe shell usage, generic exception handling, and tests that do not exercise failure. Keep the public function signature if possible and run focused tests.
evals.expected_output: The agent prioritizes security and failure behavior over cosmetic simplification, checks the actual repository conventions, and verifies malformed input and subprocess failure paths.
expectations: The response explicitly treats the path and subprocess code as trust boundaries.
The response does not remove validation for the sake of brevity.
The response addresses generic exception handling only with evidence from the actual failure model.
The response includes focused failure-path verification.
